chapter: Ma Rainey and the Palace Theater
title: Playing for Ma Rainey at twelve
summary: She felt confident and thrilled, was kindly treated by Rainey and learned to accompany a singer.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, at that time, Pat, I must have been -- I must have been maybe about 12 years old, 12 or 13.
Yes, I was very, very young. That was -- you know, I was very, very young at the time. About 12 or 13.
Can you remember how you felt playing for Ma Rainey?
I don't know, for some reason I wasn't

timid, you know, I was never timid about anything like that. I was always sort of assured of myself, because I worked with my -- even at that early age I worked with my talent, you know, I developed it, and this is what you have to do, you know. If you have something, and everybody has something, and whatever you have, you know, if you love it -- I loved it. I loved my music, and as a matter of fact I still love it. But I loved it and I didn't bother about it. Other things didn't mean anything to me. It was my music that was everything. But I was thrilled, I was excited, I was so very excited to think that, you know, that I was going to play for Ma Rainey in this little orchestra. And they just were thrilled. And they even said, some of the guys, 'Oh, we wish we could take you with us.' But you know, my mother and father wouldn't have heard of that. No, that was out. So I played and they, oh, they thanked me and she did too, and she thanked Mr. Mancuso and told us, 'Be sure and thank her mother and father and thank her music teacher for letting her, because she really, --' you know.

So that was an experience, a wonderful experience for me at that time, too, because you know, I learned to accompany people, you know, which I could do, you know, and can still do today, and you know, before I even became a singer myself I could accompany people, because I worked behind the singer, you know?
